newsitem.title: PERU: Peru bishop confirms MRTA leader in talks.
newsitem.headline: Peru bishop confirms MRTA leader in talks.

text.p: Roman Catholic archbishop Juan Luis Cipriani confirmed that Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) leader Nestor Cerpa Cartolini had attended Thursday's talks on the Peruvian hostage crisis with government negotiator Domingo Palermo.

Cerpa and MRTA number two, Rolly Rojas, alias "The Arab," took part in the talks, which will continue on Monday, Cipriani told reporters after the meeting. It was the first time that Cerpa had left the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence during the 65-day-old hostage crisis.

Conversations took place in a "constructive atmosphere" and dealt with "various important issues which will require in depth analysis," Cipriani added in a Spanish-language statement that was read out afterwards in English by Canada's ambassador Anthony Vincent.
Cipriani, Vincent and Red Cross representative Michel Minnig are all members of a guarantors' commission overseeing the talks. Japanese government observer Terusuke Terada also attended the talks.
The meeting followed last week's three rounds of face-to- face talks that broke a previous deadlock in the crisis.
The MRTA is holding 72 hostages taken in the Dec. 17 storming of the diplomatic compound.
